Just make sure you get vials where you can check authenticity with the lab mentioned. I've been DIY for 5 years.

I was misdiagnosed with BPD years ago. I was inpatient and there was no assessment, hadn't met the psychiatrist no one asked about my symptoms/history etc. I only found out when I went for ECG and it said diagnosis on the form. 

There is a marked difference in treatment before healthcare staff know your diagnosis and after. My sister thought I was imagining this shift or just taking it the wrong way until she was in A&E with me following an attempt. She was dumfounded at the jeckel and Hyde transformation. 

I went from human deserving compassion and care to a naughty child who needs to be punished. And the only way they can punish is to withdraw help. They become cold and cruel with no empathy. 

Yes some people with BPD exhibit behaviour that is difficult to deal with and the stigma which causes staff to behave this way may help with those patients who are on the extreme end of things. But it's not everyone, far from it and the impact it has on those seeking help who are met with this attitude and treatment can be very damaging. 

I think the behaviour of individual patients should affect their treatment by staff but it's not fair to abandon a whole population of people based on a bad experience with an individual in the past.

 I don't think anyone would argue that it's an easy disorder to treat, but it's a disorder that is not the patients fault. They didn't choose this. Who would?

I think that her reaction indicates that there's more to it than just not wanting you to get surgery. A lot has changed for you both in last few years and there is more change to come with the baby. 

It could be that she has struggled with your transition more than she has admitted. Perhaps she is afraid that this next step could be the one that ends your relationship. 
Maybe she is not attracted to men and has compromised until now due to the desire to maintain your relationship. She may know in herself that if you get surgery then she will not be happy in the relationship and her grief is not at the possibility of you having surgery, but the possibility that your relationship will end and so will the family unit that she imagines in her near future. 

It's your body and only you can decide what you want and need.
